label: Blancmange
note: Milk or cream and sugar thickened with rice flour, gelatin or cornflour, often almond flavoured, set in a mould; medieval ones had shredded capon; traces back to the older Middle Eastern muhallebi

about.text: A sweet European dessert of milk or cream, sugar and a thickener, usually set in a mould and served cold.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: The cornflour is stirred smooth in a little cold milk, then into the hot sweetened milk. Boiling gelatinises the starch, which then sets to a gel as it cools. Home recipes differ a lot in proportions; Wikipedia gives no numbers.

steps.note: Bay leaf or lemon peel in the hot milk.
2 tablespoons, mixed with 1/4 cup of the cold milk first.
Brought to the boil, then simmered.

steps.name: set
steps.note: In a mould rinsed with cold water, chilled until set.
